newsitem.title: USA: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 6.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Wall Street Journal - Sept 6.

text.p: Federal Reserve officials are worried that the new increase in the federal minimum wage will boost inflation, The Wall Street Journal reported on Friday.
The concern over inflation may influence their deliberations on whether to raise interest rates this month.

Several central bank officials said this week their analysis showed the $0.50 increase in the minimum wage that takes place on October 1 could boost average hourly earnings at an annual rate of 0.8 percent in the fourth quarter.

The higher minimum wage comes at a time when labour markets are very tight and the economy is already operating near its full capacity, and as a result it could complicate the Fed's efforts to stay ahead of inflation.
* A surprise downturn in claims for first time unemployment benefits raises concerns about Friday's August payroll report.
* General Motors Corp's Hughes Electronics Corp unit is pursuing two satellite deals with a potential price tag of nearly $4 billion.
* British pharmaceutical manufacturer SmithKline Beecham Plc is close to an agreement to pay more than $300 million to the U.S. government to settle billing charges.
* Summit Technology Inc founder and chief executive David Muller is fired.
* The National Transportation Safety Board is readying safety recommendations affecting Boeing Co's 737 and 757 airliners.
* Shares of Campbell Soup Co hit record high on news of layoffs, acquisition and stock buyback.
* Dow Jones Industrial Average falls 49.94 point to 5,606.96.
* Retailers had mixed results during August.
